Vexl1nar4731
The Creation of Voxelia

Vexl1nar4731 from the ages of 16 to 19, so 3 years, spent time creating the Roblox game Voxelia all by himself. What does Voxelia entail? Well, it is a very massive world (Earth-sized) and features many biomes and it is so detailed that there are analogues to Dallol, Ethiopia and Socotra, Yemen found throughout the map. It has an equal ratio of ocean to land and also features a sandbox aspect: You mine for resources and it features the entire periodic table of elements that occur naturally when he first made it. There are also dungeons, animals, mobs, mythical/legendary creatures. Also, the game features progression, you get armour, you get weapons etc. 

The game also features space exploration: You can make a spaceship with a lot of materials you mine, the materials being similar to how you make real spaceships and you can explore the Moon, which has resources on lunar craters, but is relatively boring like our own Moon. It also has Venus and Jupiter counterparts which are meant to be like the hellish and heavenly worlds of this game. It also has the heavenly world being far bigger than the Earthly world and also has the hellish world being the same size as the earthly world, sort of similar to real life. 

Not only that, the game also features modern weaponry in addition to simple weapons and armour ala Minecraft. Keep in mind, the game is singleplayer, so only one player can be on a server and keep in mind it is on Roblox, despite its vast detail. Immediately upon release, the game surged in popularity and well at the beginning of the story, it has over 100 000 players, which shows how successful it is and the ability of Vex to understand what would get people to play his game.

(FRI, VSI, WMI, Abstract Reasoning, Inductive Reasoning, Intuition, Mental Fortitude, Cognitive Discipline, Emotional Understanding, Social Awareness, Anticipation, Perception, Planning, Decision-Making)
Noticing the Entity for the First Time

As Vex was walking down through a maze while playing his game Voxelia, he noticed only for like a second at best, since he had walked away and only told of him having seen something odd after exiting the maze. What he saw was a slightly different shade of grey on just a single line of the maze’s wall. 

Knowing something was off about his game, him knowing 100% that a single line was not meant to be different, he checks the server list and notices that there is no one. That is normal since it is meant to be singleplayer. He then goes to Roblox Studio to change it but cannot, thus realizing it is at the level of the code. When he scrolls through the code, it does not appear like he noticed anything, but he then says that something changed and it was likely a subtle thing, as it is remarked that whatever did this was good at hiding.

(VSI, PSI, Perception, FRI, Observation, WMI, Inductive Reasoning, Abductive Reasoning, Abstract Reasoning, Mental Fortitude)

Lua Interpreter Trap

Wanting to test whether this entity is just a hacker or is something much deeper, like a fundamental glitch or code, that is sentient. He undoes the changes that the Entity does, but he knows that he will not be available 24/7 to watch over his game in case the Entity decides to mess with it. 

So Vexl1nar4731 decides to set up a detector, which has the role of detecting changes to his game’s code. He knows not to do it within the game code of the game because if it is a hacker, said hacker can just mess with it. As such, he sets it up outside of his game’s code. He knows that if the entity were to be living within the computer code itself, like just the computer in general, it would have access to the detector and nullify it still. 

As a back up to his Lua Interpreter, he also creates his own local script and encodes all the logic into a mesh. He is doing this to 100% eliminate the concept of it being a hacker if it is actually an entity, cuz he knows that a hacker just would not be able to overcome this code detector, due to how complex it is, however something living in his computer would be able to because it sees the fundamental data, plus a hacker would have no knowledge that such a code detector is made, while something that is inside his computer would. 

When he checks the detector, it seems like it detected the right sort of changes, but when he compares the game code, looking really carefully, he notices that the detector detected changes but the wrong sort of changes. In Vex’s eyes this is bad news because he did not confront a hacker, but rather he confronted or is confronting a sentient digital entity and while the Entity tried to be subtle about it, Vex still managed to detect it.

(Abductive Reasoning, Planning, Strategy, Trap Setting, Foresight, FRI, WMI, VSI, Learning Capacity, Mental Fortitude, Cognitive Discipline, Stress Tolerance)

Intranet Trap

Vexl1nar4731 realizes that he will never be able to go toe to toe with the Entity in raw intellect, so he decides to tap into what makes him human. The setbacks, the unpredictability of humans in the eyes of machines and his realization that despite the fact that the Entity’s mind is far more powerful than his is, he has a human element that it can never have. In addition to this, he also knows the Entity is not confined to his home computer, because of what he had done after school with the whole Python code. So with this information, he comes up with an idea.

That idea is to have the code detector be on a separate computer and not just any computer, but an intranet, a local network, completely isolated from the others, reasoning that the Entity cannot be inside such a network by its very nature. As such, Vexl1nar4731 spends almost a day building a computer that functions based on an intranet and he also makes sure to buy components through offline means (using cash, buying components physically from stores etc.), so as to not alarm the Entity in any way, because it does not have access to the offline. 

Meanwhile, he also spends time creating a .bin file on his regular computer, which he does not always update, like only sporadically at irregular intervals of time, so as to make the Entity not fall for any tricks. The script looks unconventional, nothing like an actual code detector, even though it is, so the Entity cannot assume much from it. When he finishes up both the intranet and the .bin file by the end of that day, he decides to begin the transfer process that will happen completely irregularly, like at irregular time intervals, switching from USBs to SSDs and SD cards at will, not in any specific order or time interval. Eventually, he finally finishes the transfer of the code detector into the Intranet and immediately deletes the .bin file from his regular computer, leaving it only on the Intranet, for he has everything he needs to make the code detector on it already, even if it is on an intranet. 

When he goes to check, the Entity has not changed or messed with the code at all. Vex decides to check the code very deeply and plays the game to spot changes, yet he still does not see anything, so the only thing he can conclude now is that the Entity is not changing the code because it knows it will be detected and it will not be able to do anything about it, however it realized it too late, since the detector is already on the Intranet, outside of its reach.

So yea, Vex would have had to know just from looking at it that it was not the right prime number and not only that he knew which was the right prime number from the fake prime number despite the very high value of it, in the billions. Knowing mentally that such a large number is prime cannot work with just pure guess work, so he likely had to either somehow remember it, immediately make the math in his mind to prove it is prime or he somehow got lucky, which is very unlikely.

E-Mail Solving Feat

Vexl1nar4731 receives an e-mail from his old buddy in the NSA, John E. Hostetler. He obviously notices it is not in English but rather it is in cipher, it is code and that he has to decode it. When he opened the link, he was led to a video of a logic puzzle that went like this:

“In a room there are several sacks. The number of sacks is not known, but it can be any number greater than three. In each of those bags there are several apples. The number of apples is also not known, but it can be any number greater than three. One sack of apples is full of fresh apples, the rest are rotten apples. A rotten apple weighs 90g, while a fresh apple weighs 100g. 

You have a scale that you can use to weigh the apples from the sacks. You also have an indicator, telling you the weight of the items you measured. If you insert an apple, you will get its weight. But that indicator will only show you the weight of say an apple if you insert one token and you can only insert one, so only one result. 

You can put apples on the scale all you want, but keep in mind, you have only one token, only one chance to figure out the weight. 

So what is your task? Well, you have to find out the bag that contains fresh apples using just one weighting, just one use of the scale. Good luck!”
